scope: All 191 Part 1 candidates, Part 2 agent-workspace verdicts, shared-helper plan. Static trace of every entry, dynamic coverage as documented; blocked entries are not validated fixes.

findings.title: Reject failed or interrupted provider turns
findings.claim: A `turn/completed` notification does not necessarily mean success: the pinned contract allows `/params/turn/status` to be `completed`, `interrupted`, or `failed` (`schemas/codex-app-server/0.146.0/ServerNotification.json:6912-6918`).
findings.evidence: provider/codex_app_server.rs parse_provider_event compares status to completed; provider.rs drive_turn refuses !completed. Interrupted and failed notifications cannot complete runs.

findings.title: Preserve approval details before asking the user
findings.claim: When Codex requests command, file-change, network, or permission approval, this replaces the request-specific command, path, reason, and permission scope with the same generic sentence.
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Preserve notifications queued before the turn loop
findings.claim: If Codex emits a notification before an `initialize`, `thread/*`, or `turn/start` response, `CodexBridge::read_until_response` removes it from stdout and stores it in `notifications`; this loop then reads only `next_raw_event()` and never drains that queue.
findings.evidence: tools/codex-bridge-spike/src/lib.rs next_raw_event pops notifications before reading stdout, preserving queued order.

findings.title: Cancel pending approvals during startup recovery
findings.claim: When the service restarts while a run is blocked, this marks the run `interrupted` but leaves its `agent_approvals` rows pending.
findings.evidence: recovery.rs selects recovering alongside starting/working/blocked, excludes unstarted work, cancels approvals transactionally on interruption; main.rs also calls cancel_terminal_run_approvals.

findings.title: Reconcile runs already marked recovering
findings.claim: If the service stops after committing the transition to `recovering` but before committing the terminal recovery result, the next startup excludes that run from this query.
findings.evidence: recovery.rs selects recovering alongside starting/working/blocked, excludes unstarted work, cancels approvals transactionally on interruption; main.rs also calls cancel_terminal_run_approvals.

findings.title: Route pre-response approvals through the application
findings.claim: If Codex emits a command or file-change approval request before the `turn/start` response, this call is still inside `CodexBridge::read_until_response`, which handles such server requests through `respond_to_server_request` and immediately returns `{"decision"
findings.evidence: Production codex_app_server.rs bridge configuration disables automatic_server_request_responses. Pre-response approval requests fail closed, rather than being automatically approved. Routing them gracefully remains a separate functional limitation.

findings.title: Reject retries while the provider turn is unresolved
findings.claim: When the predecessor was interrupted because recovery observed an `inProgress` or otherwise ambiguous provider turn, `reusable_retry_workspace` checks only Git state and this call reaches `provider::start_run`, which unconditionally resumes the existing provid
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Record the new pinned provider response contract
findings.claim: This makes recovery correctness depend on `thread/read` returning `thread.turns[].id`, but the commit leaves `docs/compatibility/codex-app-server.md` unchanged.
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Extend the lease beyond the credentialed network operation
findings.claim: When token creation, remote-ref inspection, or the push takes more than 30 seconds, the one-second worker loop marks this still-running job stale here and allows another worker to reclaim it.
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Require publication by the selected Agent Run
findings.claim: When a terminal run is retried, the scheduler reuses its predecessor's Repository Workspace, but the workspace's `published_commit` is not cleared.
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Restrict merge-SHA fallback to merged close deliveries
findings.claim: Because `merge_commit_sha` is retained for every `pull_request` and `pull_request_review` action, a delayed open, synchronize, or review job can run after the PR merges.
findings.evidence: github.rs bounded_job_payload retains merge_commit_sha only for closed+merged pull_request events; reconcile_merge_commit_identity requires live REST merged state. Existing tests cover synchronize/review events.

findings.title: Pass --dbname to pg_restore
findings.claim: Under the documented restore path this runs the `agent-workspace-pg-restore` wrapper as `pg_restore --exit-on-error --no-owner --no-privileges` with the dump on stdin, but never supplies `--dbname`/`-d`.
findings.evidence: tools/host-maintenance/src/lib.rs restore supplies --dbname= with PGDATABASE. The fake pg_restore regression verifies the environment and argument order.

findings.title: Sanitize audit FKs when omitting credential rows
findings.claim: On hosts that have processed MCP bearer or OAuth requests, retained `audit_events` rows can contain `mcp_credential_id`/`mcp_oauth_grant_id` values populated by `apps/server/src/mcp/writes.rs`, and those columns are foreign keys to `mcp_client_credentials` and
findings.evidence: tools/host-maintenance/src/lib.rs sanitizer nulls session_id, mcp_credential_id and mcp_oauth_grant_id before restoring post-data; regression asserts the complete SQL.

findings.title: Clear all excluded audit foreign keys before post-data
findings.claim: When the backup contains MCP bearer or OAuth audit rows, this sanitizer only nulls `session_id`; the server also records `audit_events.mcp_credential_id` and `audit_events.mcp_oauth_grant_id` for MCP activity, while `mcp_client_credentials` and `mcp_oauth_gran
findings.evidence: Same audit-FK defect as AW-013; the sanitizer already nulls all three excluded foreign keys.

findings.title: Skip symlinks during storage admission
findings.claim: When any managed worktree contains a repository symlink, this check makes `require_growth` return a storage conflict before starting runs or preparing repositories, even if quota and free-space watermarks are healthy.
findings.evidence: storage_admission.rs skips descendant symlinks and has symlinks_are_skipped_without_following_targets. Root-symlink bypass is separately tracked as AW-069.

findings.title: Preserve ignored files before removing worktrees
findings.claim: When a retained worktree contains only files ignored by Git, `inspect_worktree` reports it clean because `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` does not list ignored files unless `--ignored` is used; I also verified `git worktree remove` deletes such a
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Preserve the OAuth grant's approved scopes
findings.claim: When an agent connection has broader permissions than the OAuth request (for example, the connection has `write` but the user approved only `read`), this branch replaces `grant_row.scopes` with the connection's full scope list.
findings.evidence: mcp/oauth.rs agent_grant_scopes strips mutating scopes from read-only consent, but full consent deliberately uses the agent connection permissions. Scope response wording and exact full-scope semantics need a product decision; no silent change.

findings.title: Keep webhook signing keys out of database records
findings.claim: The new `webhook_secret` column stores every HMAC signing key as plaintext, and the delivery worker reads that value back to sign requests.
findings.evidence: external_agents.rs writes encrypted webhook_secret_id and NULL plaintext on create/rotate; secrets startup migration handles legacy plaintext when keyring exists. Old deployment without a master key remains an operator migration prerequisite.

findings.title: Reject private webhook destinations
findings.claim: A project owner or admin can configure any syntactically valid HTTP(S) URL, after which the server performs POST requests to it from the background worker.
findings.evidence: replies.rs validates HTTPS public destinations, validates all resolved addresses and pins checked DNS; exact trusted origins are operator-configured. No project-manager exception authorizes arbitrary private addresses.

findings.title: Keep webhook signing secrets out of browser responses
findings.claim: When a manager configures a webhook through the settings endpoint, this serializes the new signing key into the HTTP response, and the frontend subsequently renders it in the page.
findings.evidence: external_agents.rs returns a newly generated signing key once to its authorized manager; read views omit it. One-time issuance versus the broad no-browser-secrets wording needs an explicit policy decision.

findings.title: Recheck visibility when loading private reply metadata
findings.claim: For a members-only DM or group, the timeline access check and this reply-metadata load run as separate pool operations, while `timeline_requests` accepts no viewer and reads the conversation by raw ID without `conversation_visible_to`.
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Keep human project and organization roles aligned
findings.claim: When an owner promotes an existing human from `member` to `admin`, this path now updates only `project_memberships`; the removed `sync_organization_role` call leaves their organization role as `member`.
findings.evidence: memberships.rs calls sync_organization_role in the same transaction; explicit/custom workspace roles are preserved intentionally.

findings.title: Authorize approvals against the selected project
findings.claim: For an approval created in an agent's additional project, `approval_get` and `approval_respond` cannot succeed: this resolver has no `approvalId` lookup, and even when the caller supplies the newly exposed `projectId`, `mcp/approvals.rs` still joins the projec
findings.evidence: mcp.rs PRIMARY_SCOPES resolves approvalId to its target project. mcp/approvals.rs loads that project, current organization membership and agent_connection_can_access. NULL-run approvals remain a separate functional gap, not this cross-project claim.

findings.title: Authorize sponsored runs in the resolved project
findings.claim: When `external_execution_request_create` targets a conversation in an additional project, this new lookup changes `principal.project_id` to that project, but `external_execution.rs` still requires `credential.project_id = principal.project_id` and joins the me
findings.evidence: external_execution.rs uses the resolved conversation project and agent_connection_can_access, while credentials remain anchored to the home project.

findings.title: Parse resource URLs before resolving their project
findings.claim: The new tools advertise canonical links as valid identifiers, but this middleware only resolves `pageId`, `threadId`, and similar fields when the entire value parses as a UUID.
findings.evidence: mcp/common.rs parse_id accepts UUIDs and canonical trailing-UUID links; middleware uses it. Some handler-level parsers remain UUID-only, a separate functional cleanup.

findings.title: Require current organization membership to manage agent grants
findings.claim: When a person’s organization membership is disabled but their project membership remains enabled, this branch still treats them as an owner/admin of the agent’s OAuth grant, allowing them to toggle or revoke a connected app after losing access to the organizat
findings.evidence: connected_apps.rs owned_grant joins enabled organization_memberships for the manager, so leftover project membership is insufficient.

findings.title: Enforce read-only access for agent grants
findings.claim: When a client requests write access but the user selects an agent and chooses the newly offered Read only option, this stores only `read` on the grant, but `resolve_access_token` later replaces those grant scopes with the agent connection's scopes.
findings.evidence: mcp/oauth.rs agent_grant_scopes keeps only read/events for read-only consent and has an explicit read-only-consent regression.

findings.title: Wait for the claimed WorkOS session check
findings.claim: When two requests arrive after a WorkOS session’s five-minute check expires, the first request sets `workos_checked_at` while contacting WorkOS, but the second loses the conditional update and this branch authenticates it immediately.
findings.evidence: auth/workos.rs conditional UPDATE claims one provider check; concurrent requests deliberately retain the session until the check resolves. Fail-closed waiting changes latency and availability policy.

findings.title: Reject ambiguous project keys before archiving
findings.claim: When an account-wide user belongs to two organizations containing the same project key, this query returns both IDs in unspecified order but then silently selects the first.
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Reject ambiguous task keys before rewriting IDs
findings.claim: For an account-wide caller with access to two organizations that both have, for example, `AW-1`, both rows satisfy this query because project keys are only organization-scoped.
findings.evidence: Reviewed and revised PR #211. task_by_key now groups by task ID before LIMIT 2, and resolve_among distinguishes missing, unique and ambiguous lookup results. It keeps the archived-original fallback for an unreadable moved target, but cannot use it after an ambiguous shared lookup. historical_aliases_cannot_hide_a_conflicting_task_key covers a current key and two historical alias rows across workspaces.

findings.title: Check current org membership for archived projects
findings.claim: For an account-wide OAuth grant whose organization membership has been disabled while its project-membership row remains enabled, `includeArchived` still adds that organization's archived project IDs because this query checks only `project_memberships`.
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Recheck access to the actual move target
findings.claim: When retrying an archived source UUID, the caller only needs access to the supplied `toProjectId`, which may be an unrelated project; `already_moved` then returns the current key, title, and URL from the actual destination without checking current access to th
findings.evidence: mcp/task_move.rs already_moved filters the actual destination with actor_can_access_project and projects_showing_tasks; it does not trust the supplied destination alone.

findings.title: Recheck conversation visibility inside the write transaction
findings.claim: For a non-thread conversation, access is checked by `record_visible` on a separate pool connection before this transaction starts, while this query omits `conversation_visible_to`; if the caller is removed from the private conversation between those operations
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Route thread lookups through conversation visibility
findings.claim: Apply `conversation_visible_to` to this removal-time thread lookup (and the related thread queries in this helper) rather than querying `conversations` directly.
findings.evidence: message_edits.rs removal paths enter through lock_message_for_change and the locked origin conversation. Child lookups are structurally limited to threads of that origin; lack of a repeated literal predicate does not itself establish the claimed leak.

findings.title: Apply PR visibility to browser work-item reads
findings.claim: This predicate is not applied by the browser work-item projection: `WORK_ITEM_BY_ID_SELECT` in `apps/server/src/work_items.rs` still aggregates every row from `github_pull_request_work_item_links` without `pull_request_visible_to`.
findings.evidence: work_items.rs WORK_ITEM_SELECT linked-PR aggregation applies pull_request_visible_to and work_item_view suppresses code details when code permission is absent.

findings.title: Bound DNS resolution before blocking the reply worker
findings.claim: When an external agent configures a hostname whose DNS resolution stalls, this `lookup_host` await is outside `WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT`, which only applies after the reqwest client is built.
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Preserve the deployed private wakeup target
findings.claim: The documented live Nyx receiver is `100.119.56.3:8732` (`docs/plans/workspace-merge-plan.md:27-30`), which lies in the 100.64/10 range rejected here.
findings.evidence: replies.rs already has exact-origin trusted webhook configuration, including tests for the tailnet address. Blanket CGNAT acceptance would change SSRF protection; deployment must configure its specific trusted origin.

findings.title: Clear drafts whenever the authenticated session ends
findings.claim: This clears local drafts only after an explicit logout request succeeds.
findings.evidence: auth/session.ts logout clears local drafts before awaiting the request. Session expiry detaches the draft owner; owner-scoped storage retains the same person offline outbox. Erasing that outbox on expiry is a product policy change.

findings.title: Keep reset tokens off workspace-controlled SMTP
findings.claim: When a person belongs to a workspace whose owner controls its SMTP endpoint, and their preferred workspace has no configured mail, this query selects that owner-controlled transport for password-reset messages.
findings.evidence: Locally incorporated reviewed PR #211 commits 7cd01f8 and 9de9350, with authorship retained. See PR-211-review.md for the per-item code trace, tests and limits. Full local verification is recorded separately; this is not a claim that main or the remote PR was changed.

findings.title: Account for preview images before storing them
findings.claim: When link previews are enabled and messages reference unique pages with images, this writes each processed image under the file-store directory without calling `require_room`.
findings.evidence: link_previews.rs fetch_job calls files::require_room before storing images; files accounting includes link_previews.image_bytes.

findings.title: Avoid granting a permanent branch during refresh grace
findings.claim: When a stolen refresh token is replayed within five minutes of its legitimate exchange, this branch issues the attacker a new refresh token whose `used_at` is null and whose lifetime is another 30 days.
findings.evidence: mcp/oauth.rs refresh grace still issues a live replacement refresh token. Shortening grace-issued expiry or access-only responses can overwrite a shared client token store with an unusable answer. Explicitly deferred by assignment; preserve pending Mischa decision.

findings.title: Keep bearer tokens out of traced URL paths
findings.claim: Whenever an app submits a report, the bearer secret occupies the `{token}` path segment, while the global `TraceLayer` in `lib.rs` records `request.uri().path()` for every request.
findings.evidence: lib.rs logged_path uses MatchedPath, so bug-report bearer paths log /api/v1/bug-reports/{token}; raw secret is not the traced path.

findings.title: Stub the new pinned-Node check in the CI area test fixture
findings.claim: Adding this step breaks every CI run that includes Rust: `AreaValidationTests.setUp()` creates a temporary checkout and stubs `test_admission.sh`, but does not provide `tools/ci/test_pinned_node.sh`.
findings.evidence: tools/ci/test_areas.py stubs test_pinned_node.sh and asserts it was dispatched. Current checks.sh validates areas before execution.

findings.title: Enforce task-view permissions when reading task attachments
findings.claim: When a caller retains a task attachment's file ID after losing `tasks.view`, `file_read` still returns its contents.
findings.evidence: files.rs READABLE task branch requires tasks.view in the target project, with hidden_by_agent_limit applied afterward. roles_and_access::task_files_follow_who_can_see_tasks covers the path.

findings.title: Apply agent limits when authorizing task-comment moderation
findings.claim: When an app acting for an Admin retains `tasks.view` and `tasks.edit` but excludes `channels.moderate`, `task_comment_delete` can still delete another person's comment.
findings.evidence: work_items/comments.rs is_comment_moderator checks agent_limit_hides ChannelsModerate before custom-role moderation. Regression an_app_moderates_only_within_its_agent_limit exists.

findings.title: Avoid promoting custom project invitees to workspace Admin
findings.claim: When an owner invites someone to a custom Admin-based project role that excludes `members.invite` or `roles.manage`, `accept_new_user` still creates an unrestricted Admin organization membership before storing this custom project role.
findings.evidence: invitations.rs separates custom role_id from built-in Admin, constrains issuance by require_grantable and accept-time issuer_still_grants. roles_and_access has custom-admin invitation regressions.

findings.title: Bound OAuth agent credential issuance by grantable permissions
findings.claim: When a narrowed administrator retains `agents.manage` but lacks `tasks.edit`, they can still connect an OAuth client as an existing unrestricted Member agent.
findings.evidence: mcp/oauth.rs managed_agent bounds the agent grant by both manager standing and project_holding. roles_and_access::connecting_an_app_as_an_agent_stays_within_the_project_role covers narrowed project roles.

findings.title: Check project management permission before propagating roles
findings.claim: When a workspace Admin lacks `members.manage` in a project through a custom project role or project-specific agent limit, they can still change another member's role there by calling `role_assign` with `applyToProjects: true`.
findings.evidence: roles.rs apply_to_their_projects authorizes MembershipManage through manage_refusal per target and checks grant subset of project_holding; inaccessible projects are skipped.

findings.title: Enforce one active run per execution profile
findings.claim: When two Threads use the same execution profile, this guard checks only `conversation_id`, so both runs can start separate App Server processes against the same retained `CODEX_HOME`.
findings.evidence: scheduler.rs now admits against provider_account max_concurrent_runs and one active turn per conversation; pooled adapters own account concurrency. Restoring the old one-process-per-profile restriction would conflict with the current provider-account design.

findings.title: Persist provider-start failures in the visible timeline
findings.claim: When Codex fails during spawn, initialization, thread resume/start, or turn start, this records only a `run_state_changed` event that is never linked into `conversation_entries`.
findings.evidence: scheduler.rs fail_run inserts run_failed plus a conversation entry, retains worktree and publishes an update. Provider-start failures use this path.

findings.title: Handle queued runs before entering recovery
findings.claim: If startup finds a legitimate `created` or `queued` run, both of which this query explicitly selects, `transition_run(..., Recovering)` rejects the transition because the state table permits recovery only from `starting`, `working`, or `blocked`.
findings.evidence: recovery.rs first clears leases for created/queued work, then selects only started states and recovering. Unstarted work returns to scheduler admission.

findings.title: Recover from an unresumable provider session
findings.claim: When a retained provider Thread is no longer available—for example after its `CODEX_HOME` is reset or corrupted—`thread/resume` fails here, but the unique `provider_sessions` mapping remains unchanged.
findings.evidence: provider.rs still propagates resume_thread failure while retaining the provider_sessions mapping. A safe reset/replacement flow needs a lost-provider-history regression and a user-visible continuity policy; no such change is included.

findings.title: Enforce the ten-character Project key limit
findings.claim: Tighten the existing `projects` check constraint in this migration.
findings.evidence: Migration 0003_m0_consistency.sql tightens projects_project_key_check to ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}$, which supersedes the initial migration quoted by the finding.

findings.title: Acquire parent and child Conversation locks in one order
findings.claim: When a Message send or Thread archive overlaps with archiving its parent Channel, this path first holds the child `FOR UPDATE` lock and then waits for the parent `FOR SHARE` lock, while `archive_conversation` holds the parent first and then locks every child.
findings.evidence: conversations.rs lock_conversation_scope obtains project, then parent, then child locks and rechecks visibility after waits; writes enter through lock_conversation_for/lock_message_conversation.

findings.title: Enforce or paginate the active Channel limit
findings.claim: Once a Project has more than 100 active Channels, this alphabetical `LIMIT` silently omits at least one Channel from the sidebar, while `create_channel` continues accepting additional Channels and the endpoint exposes no cursor.
findings.evidence: conversations.rs lists at most MAX_CHANNELS_PER_PROJECT=100 while channel creation is not capped. Correcting the product behavior requires choosing a write cap or paginated channel navigation; no silent channel-admission restriction added.

findings.title: Paginate Threads before building the sidebar projection
findings.claim: For Projects with more than 1,000 Threads, the global `LIMIT` discards older rows before grouping and projection.
findings.evidence: conversations.rs sidebar query still applies a global MAX_THREADS_PER_SIDEBAR=1000 before grouping. Complete per-channel pagination and large-project regressions are not implemented in this branch.

findings.title: Expose failure acknowledgement outside the worker composer
findings.claim: For a Viewer, `ReadStateUpdate` is allowed while `WorkerInvoke` is denied (`policy.rs`), so the server reports an unacknowledged failure and permits its acknowledgement, but this button is nested inside `showComposer`, which is false unless `workerInvoke` is a
findings.evidence: The failure acknowledgement is now a RunCardActions button in ThreadRunControls.tsx, outside RunComposer. The old showComposer nesting no longer controls it.

findings.title: Mint a separate token for each GitHub operation
findings.claim: During every publication, the token already used for the pre-push `branch_commit` request is cloned here into the Git child and then retained for the post-push `branch_commit` request.
findings.evidence: github.rs publication still uses one repository-scoped installation token for ref inspection, push and confirmation, all parts of the same explicit publication operation. Per-HTTP-request credential minting changes rate/credential lifetime policy without demonstrating a new authority grant.

findings.title: Project an existing pull request onto retry runs
findings.claim: Retry runs can reuse the predecessor's `repository_workspace_id`, while pull-request requests are unique per workspace and the create endpoint returns that existing request.
findings.evidence: conversations.rs and run_views.rs still join github_pull_request_requests by agent_run_id, while retry reuse keeps a workspace identity. Showing an existing workspace PR on retries requires a shared projection change and retry/PR integration regression; absent here.

findings.title: Exclude archived Work Items from pull-request creation
findings.claim: When a Thread retains a link to an archived Work Item, the timeline still includes that item with a non-null `archivedAt`, but this request submits every linked ID.
findings.evidence: useThreadRunActions.tsx still sends every linkedWorkItems ID to PR creation, including archived chips. A create-PR regression for mixed active/archived links is not yet included; no claim that PR #211 covers it.

findings.title: Serialize recovery before locking the job
findings.claim: When two exact redeliveries concurrently target the same failed or exhausted job, both transactions can first acquire `FOR SHARE` on the delivery at line 4442; one then locks the job here while the other waits for that job, after which the first blocks trying
findings.evidence: github.rs exact redelivery reads checksum without the old delivery FOR SHARE lock, then updates failed/exhausted jobs before updating delivery. The specific two-shared-lock upgrade deadlock is absent.

findings.title: Load the systemd environment without shell evaluation
findings.claim: When a service value contains shell metacharacters—for example `$$` in the database password—systemd's `EnvironmentFile=` in `deploy/redhat/agent-workspace.service:14` passes it literally, while `source` expands it as Bash syntax under root.
findings.evidence: deploy/redhat/agent-workspace-service-command still sources the root-owned EnvironmentFile as Bash. Exact systemd EnvironmentFile parsing and wrapper parity tests are needed; a partial shell parser would be unsafe.

findings.title: Relax parent permission checks for restore roots
findings.claim: When running the documented clean restore drill with `--target-data-root /var/lib/agent-workspace-restore-drill` and `--target-release-root /opt/agent-workspace-restore-drill`, this check rejects the normal Red Hat parents because `/var/lib` and `/opt` usually
findings.evidence: Host-maintenance restore-root validation still checks directory ownership/permissions along the path. Relaxing trusted root-owned ancestors needs clean-restore fixtures and a precise trust rule; not safely changed in this pass.

findings.title: Reject unexpected data archive members
findings.claim: For `data.tar`, this validation only rejects absolute paths and parent traversal; a repacked archive with a matching manifest checksum and a member such as `codex/profiles/auth.json` or `logs/...` passes and is extracted into the restore root.
findings.evidence: tools/host-maintenance/src/lib.rs safe_archive_entry rejects absolute/traversal paths but does not restrict data archive contents to the captured runtime categories. An allowlist needs restore-format compatibility and archive-member regressions, absent here.

findings.title: Meter the board work-item read path
findings.claim: Because this budget is only applied in `list_work_items`, the existing `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/work-items/board` path still accepts the same search/filter query and runs its per-status SQL queries without consuming the expensive-read limiter.
findings.evidence: work_items.rs list and board handlers both call check_expensive_read before executing their queries.

findings.title: Count malformed OAuth attempts before extraction

findings.evidence: storage_admission.rs now skips NotFound only for descendants, including directories removed after stat; missing roots and other errors still fail. Root symlinks are refused. Regressions use real directory deletion at metadata lookup and a symlink to a populated root.

findings.evidence: provider.rs provider_approval_policy explicitly keeps execution approvals human-required while questions may target any authorized approver. Unit test provider_approval_policy_keeps_execution_approvals_human_required pins this safety policy.

findings.evidence: mcp/oauth.rs protected-resource metadata advertises workspace scopes when WorkOS is enabled, and parse_scopes normalizes workspace:read/workspace:write to local read/write. Unit regression accepts both spellings; the local server supports the advertised resource scopes.

findings.evidence: mcp/runs.rs run_value still emits /projects/{project}/threads/{conversation}, without a direct-parent route discriminator. Needs a DM/group run routing regression and shared canonical-link helper.

findings.evidence: SettingsArea project picker navigates to project settings without refreshing project lastOpenedAt, so off-rail deep links may stay hidden. Needs navigation-state regression and deciding whether opening settings counts as project use.

findings.title: Normalize the returned location for legacy clients
findings.claim: When a settings-stuck page is still running the pre-change JavaScript bundle during deployment, the switch response continues to report `location.kind` as `settings` even though this branch returns the overview href.
findings.evidence: Legacy settings navigation location normalization needs old-client projection fixtures. Current switch flow refreshes lastOpenedAt but retains stored navigation metadata; no compatibility rewrite included.

findings.title: Recompute the focus trap after the lazy sidebar mounts
findings.claim: When a user opens the mobile navigation on a cold Home or Messages load before this lazy chunk resolves, the focus-trap effect has already captured only `#project-rail` because the fallback has no `#project-sidebar`.
findings.evidence: AppShell focus effect captures drawer elements before a lazy sidebar mounts. Keyboard handling enumerates controls fresh but from those captured elements. Needs a delayed-sidebar keyboard regression and observer/ref ownership fix.

findings.title: Preserve reset tokens after ambiguous SMTP failures
findings.claim: If the SMTP server accepts the message body but the connection drops while this client waits for the final `250` reply, `mail::send` returns a retryable error even though the email may already be delivered.
findings.evidence: password_reset.rs deletes the token for every mail::send error, including ambiguous post-DATA SMTP failures. Keeping a token requires a transport-level ambiguous-acceptance regression and retry policy; no speculative credential-flow change included.

findings.title: Derive the agent catalog from its selected environment
findings.claim: When an agent has no explicit harness but has environment A selected, the environment determines its harness at launch; this code instead falls back to the project's default harness B.
findings.evidence: AgentProfileDialog runsOn uses draft.harness || project default and omits the selected environment harness. Needs a profile-with-environment/catalog regression before model defaults are normalized differently.

findings.title: Add the new route to the offline navigation allowlist
findings.claim: When an installed app reloads or directly navigates to `/design-system` while offline, the service worker does not call `openApp`: `APP_ROUTE` in `apps/web/public/sw.js` still lists `/dev` but not `/design-system`.
findings.evidence: public/sw.js APP_ROUTE includes design-system, so the renamed route is accepted for offline app navigation.

findings.title: Avoid logging unauthenticated callback probes
findings.claim: Because `/auth/workos/callback` is public, this warning also runs for requests rejected before any login attempt is validated, including a GET with missing `code` or `state`.
findings.evidence: auth/workos.rs worth_logging excludes unmatched callback stages; failure_location also receives linking, distinguishing account-link conflicts. Dedicated unit regressions cover unmatched probes and link failures.

findings.title: Distinguish link conflicts from unlinked accounts
findings.claim: When a callback was started with `link=true` but the provider subject is already linked to a different local user, `resolve_identity` also returns `AppError::Forbidden` while the step is `account`.
findings.evidence: auth/workos.rs worth_logging excludes unmatched callback stages; failure_location also receives linking, distinguishing account-link conflicts. Dedicated unit regressions cover unmatched probes and link failures.

findings.title: Clear link state when the project changes
findings.claim: When someone leaves Project A’s one-time setup card open and uses the project picker to move directly to Project B’s Bug reports page, `SettingsArea` reuses the same `BugReportsPage` instance, so `setup`, `replacing`, and `deleting` still reference A.
findings.evidence: SettingsArea.tsx keys PageBody by project.id, so switching projects remounts BugReportsPage and clears setup/replacing/deleting state. The finding did not account for this caller guard.

findings.title: Start handshake timing before authentication
findings.claim: When database or pool contention slows `resolve_bearer_principal`, or reading/parsing the request body is slow, that time counts toward the client's handshake timeout but is excluded because the timer starts only immediately before `next.run`.
findings.evidence: mcp.rs authentication middleware starts timing before bearer lookup/body read. HandshakeStep watches response bodies to distinguish JSON-RPC errors inside HTTP 200. handshake_logs_show_protocol_errors_and_the_whole_wait covers both.

findings.title: Detect protocol errors before logging handshake success
findings.claim: With the legacy-session transport configured in `router`, rmcp can carry JSON-RPC errors for `initialize` or `tools/list` inside an HTTP 200 response.
findings.evidence: mcp.rs authentication middleware starts timing before bearer lookup/body read. HandshakeStep watches response bodies to distinguish JSON-RPC errors inside HTTP 200. handshake_logs_show_protocol_errors_and_the_whole_wait covers both.

findings.title: Let task-edit permission open task attachment uploads
findings.claim: For a custom role or agent limit that retains `tasks.view` and `tasks.edit` but excludes `channels.post` everywhere, this prerequisite hides and rejects `file_upload` even when it targets a task.
findings.evidence: files upload authorization routes task attachments through TasksEdit; roles_and_access::task_files_follow_who_can_see_tasks exercises narrowed task-only roles.

findings.title: Filter task attachments from search by task-view permission
findings.claim: When a custom role or app limit excludes `tasks.view`, searching for files still exposes attachments from those projects because only `SearchKind::Tasks` receives the filtered project list.
findings.evidence: search.rs computes task_projects whenever Tasks OR Files is searched and binds that list separately for task attachment hits. file_search_leaves_out_task_files_where_tasks_are_hidden covers it.

findings.title: Filter saved task previews by current task-view permission
findings.claim: When a person has saved a task and subsequently loses `tasks.view` through a custom role or app limit, `later_list` still returns its current title, key and status.
findings.evidence: later.rs applies roles::role_allows_sql tasks.view plus agent-limit project filtering before saved task projections.

findings.title: Apply code-view restrictions to project overview repositories
findings.claim: For a custom role or app limit without `code.view`, `project_open` remains callable and returns repository IDs, owner/name pairs and default branches.
findings.evidence: mcp/briefing.rs project_open computes sees_code via projects_allowing(CodeView) before including repositories; reads_naming_tasks_or_repositories_follow_the_role_and_limit covers it.

findings.title: Filter linked code details from task reads by code-view permission
findings.claim: When a custom role or app limit retains `tasks.view` but excludes `code.view`, `task_open` still returns linked repository and pull-request details.
findings.evidence: mcp/reads.rs passes authorize_read RepositoryView into work_item_value and omits linked code without it; a_tasks_linked_code_needs_see_code covers this.

findings.title: Filter linked tasks by their own project's task-view permission
findings.claim: When a caller can view tasks in project A but lacks `tasks.view` in project B, opening an A task that depends on or relates to a B task still exposes the B task's title, key and status.
findings.evidence: mcp/planning.rs visible_links combines target-project task_links visibility, reachable projects and agent_limit_hides TasksView; linked_tasks_in_another_project_follow_see_tasks_there covers it.

findings.title: Filter usage batches by effective task-view permission
findings.claim: When a person owns a configured provider account and retains `runs.launch` but loses `tasks.view` through a custom role or app limit, `usage_batch` still returns task titles, keys and priorities.
findings.evidence: usage/batch.rs checks projects_showing_tasks for each task-bearing batch entry before naming/ranking it, applying current role and app limit.

findings.title: Filter linked pull-request details from run reads
findings.claim: When a custom role or app limit excludes `code.view`, `run_get` and `run_list` remain callable and return linked pull-request details anyway.
findings.evidence: mcp/runs.rs suppresses branch, publication-request and PR fields when projects_allowing(CodeView) rejects the target project; redaction includes row.branch.

findings.title: Preserve app attribution for batched queued launches
findings.claim: When a person's app queues multiple tasks through `task_launch`, then loses `runs.launch` before they start, these launches still execute.
findings.evidence: launch.rs persists made_through_app for queued and mention launches; drain_queued and tag jobs re-read current app limits before execution.

findings.title: Preserve app attribution for launches triggered by mentions
findings.claim: If a person's app mentions a harness-backed agent while `runs.launch` is allowed, then loses that permission before the job executes or its queued launch starts, the run still launches.
findings.evidence: launch.rs persists made_through_app for queued and mention launches; drain_queued and tag jobs re-read current app limits before execution.

findings.title: Check task-view access before returning archive results
findings.claim: When a custom project role retains `tasks.delete` but excludes `tasks.view`, a person who knows a task ID can still retrieve its full contents through the browser archive/restore endpoints.
findings.evidence: work_items.rs archive response uses capabilities TasksView to redact content. roles_and_access::archiving_without_see_tasks_reveals_no_task checks the returned view.

findings.title: Reapply app limits when queued task imports execute
findings.claim: When a person's app calls `task_import` with `commit: true` and subsequently loses `tasks.create` through its agent limit, the queued import still creates tasks.
findings.evidence: work_items/imports.rs persists made_through_app, resolves current app access and runs import chunks within_agent_limits. GitHub reads also check CodeView; role regressions cover the read path.

findings.title: Redact task details from launch cancellation responses too
findings.claim: If a person queues a task launch and subsequently loses `tasks.view`, the browser's launch-cancellation endpoint still returns the task's current key and title.
findings.evidence: launch.rs cancel returns through views_by_id, whose read projection removes work_item without sees_tasks. cancelling_a_launch_without_see_tasks_reveals_no_task covers it.

findings.title: Redact task references in comment mutation responses too
findings.claim: For a custom role that retains `tasks.edit` but excludes `tasks.view`, the browser's comment endpoints still disclose task titles and statuses because this redaction only covers `WorkItemView`.
findings.evidence: work_items/comments.rs read projection calls sees_tasks_in and removes task-reference titles when hidden; comment_references_show_titles_only_with_see_tasks covers it.

findings.title: Filter suggestion decision responses by task-view permission
findings.claim: When a custom role or app limit retains `tasks.edit` but excludes `tasks.view`, `ai_suggestion_decide` still returns restricted task details for a known pending suggestion ID.
findings.evidence: ai/suggestions.rs decision locks and checks ai_suggestion_visible_to plus WITHIN_APP_LIMIT before returning the result. ai_suggestions_need_see_tasks covers it.

findings.title: Redact task details from bulk mutation responses
findings.claim: When a custom role retains `tasks.delete` or `tasks.edit` but excludes `tasks.view`, the browser bulk endpoint still returns restricted task contents for known task UUIDs.
findings.evidence: work_items/planning.rs bulk result uses effective capabilities and strips tasks without TasksView; bulk_changes_without_see_tasks_reveal_no_task covers it.

findings.title: Check destination task visibility when replaying a move
findings.claim: When a caller can view tasks in the source project but lacks `tasks.view` in the destination, repeating `task_move` for an already-moved task returns the destination task's current title.
findings.evidence: mcp/task_move.rs already_moved filters destination titles through projects_showing_tasks; a_repeated_move_shows_the_title_only_where_tasks_are_seen covers it.

findings.title: Filter linked task titles from whiteboard reads
findings.claim: When a custom role or app limit excludes `tasks.view`, `whiteboard_read` still exposes the current titles of tasks linked to the board.
findings.evidence: whiteboards.rs resolves linked task projects through projects_showing_tasks before exposing their titles; board_links_show_task_titles_only_where_tasks_are_seen covers it.

findings.title: Enforce member-view permission on the workspace member list
findings.claim: When a custom workspace role excludes `members.view`, the browser's workspace-members endpoint still returns the member list, including roles, login names and project counts.
findings.evidence: workspace.rs list_members calls caller_may DirectoryView and otherwise returns only the caller; the_workspace_member_directory_follows_directory_view covers it.

findings.title: Require source task visibility before copying task contents
findings.claim: When a caller retains `tasks.edit` and `tasks.delete` in the source project but lacks `tasks.view`, these checks still allow moving a known task into another project where they can create and read tasks.
findings.evidence: mcp/task_move.rs requires source task visibility and CodeView for linked-code provenance. moving_a_task_needs_its_contents_and_code_to_be_seen covers both.

findings.title: Filter restricted code links from move provenance
findings.claim: When a caller can move and view tasks but lacks `code.view` in the source project, moving a task still discloses its linked repository names and pull-request URLs.
findings.evidence: mcp/task_move.rs requires source task visibility and CodeView for linked-code provenance. moving_a_task_needs_its_contents_and_code_to_be_seen covers both.

findings.title: Redact restricted task details from run-step reads
findings.claim: When a custom role or app limit excludes `tasks.view`, `run_steps` still returns the current title of a task linked to a visible run.
findings.evidence: mcp/run_pages.rs run_steps calls run_views::run_detail and run_diff; run_views::redact clears task_title when projects_showing_tasks excludes the target project.

findings.title: Redact repository branches from MCP run reads without code access
findings.claim: When a custom role or app limit excludes `code.view`, `run_get` and `run_list` still disclose `repository_workspaces.branch_name`: this helper clears only PR fields, while `run_value` returns `row.branch` unchanged.
findings.evidence: mcp/runs.rs suppresses branch, publication-request and PR fields when projects_allowing(CodeView) rejects the target project; redaction includes row.branch.

findings.title: Redact task references returned by planning mutations
findings.claim: When a custom role or app limit retains `tasks.edit` but excludes `tasks.view`, `task_relate` and `task_depend` still disclose a known task's current title and status.
findings.evidence: mcp/planning.rs mutation projections use the visibility-aware task_links path and app limit per target. link_changes_name_the_task_only_where_tasks_are_seen and link_changes_list_linked_tasks_only_where_the_app_sees_them cover it.

findings.title: Redact branches and commits from conversation run projections
findings.claim: When a custom role excludes `code.view`, opening a visible thread still returns its active or latest terminal run's repository branch, base commit and published commit.
findings.evidence: conversations.rs hide_pull_request clears branch, base_commit and published_commit as well as PR fields when code visibility is absent.

findings.title: Check task visibility before rendering a launch prompt
findings.claim: When a custom project role retains `runs.launch` and `channels.post` but excludes `tasks.view`, a person with a provider account can still launch a known task UUID through the browser launch endpoint and retrieve its contents from the resulting thread.
findings.evidence: launch.rs checks projects_showing_tasks before using a work item to render a launch prompt.

findings.title: Bound agent credential grants by the caller's project permissions
findings.claim: When a workspace Admin has a custom project role retaining `agents.manage` but excluding `code.view` or `tasks.edit`, this check still permits creating a built-in Member agent and returns its credentials.
findings.evidence: external_agents.rs require_grantable intersects manager standing with project_holding; agents_are_given_only_what_the_giver_holds_in_the_project covers it.

findings.title: Bound membership grants by the caller's project permissions
findings.claim: When a workspace Admin's custom project role retains `members.manage` but excludes `tasks.edit` or `code.view`, this helper still allows giving another member unrestricted Member access because `roles::standing` loads only the caller's workspace grant.
findings.evidence: memberships.rs require_grantable checks project_holding as well as workspace standing; project_roles_are_given_only_within_the_givers_project_role covers it.

findings.title: Recheck the project grant before accepting an invitation
findings.claim: If an administrator issues an unrestricted Member invitation and subsequently receives a custom project role without `code.view` or `tasks.edit` but retaining `members.invite`, the invitation remains redeemable with the original unrestricted grant.
findings.evidence: invitations.rs require_issuer_still_grants rechecks the issuer project grant before accept; a_project_invitation_lapses_when_its_issuers_project_role_narrows_below_it covers it.

findings.title: Check task visibility before creating a worker thread
findings.claim: When a custom project role retains `tasks.edit` and `runs.launch` but excludes `tasks.view`, the browser's `work-with-worker` endpoint still discloses a known task's current title.
findings.evidence: work_items.rs worker-thread creation checks TasksView; working_with_a_worker_needs_see_tasks covers it.

findings.title: Redact repository mutation responses without code-view access
findings.claim: When a custom project role retains `code.manage` but excludes `code.view`, the browser's repository preparation endpoint still returns restricted repository metadata for a known repository UUID.
findings.evidence: Repository prepare authorization requires RepositoryView alongside management; managing_a_repository_needs_see_code covers it.

findings.title: Bound agent OAuth grants by the manager's project permissions
findings.claim: When a workspace Admin has a custom project role retaining `agents.manage` but excluding `code.view` or `tasks.edit`, they can still authorize an OAuth client as an existing unrestricted Member agent.
findings.evidence: mcp/oauth.rs managed_agent bounds the agent grant by both manager standing and project_holding. roles_and_access::connecting_an_app_as_an_agent_stays_within_the_project_role covers narrowed project roles.

findings.title: Check the thing's own module set before returning it
findings.claim: When a person has Channels enabled in one project or workspace but disabled in another, this endpoint resolves the requested thing using the union from `state::anywhere`.
findings.evidence: modules/http.rs and mcp/module_tools.rs re-fetch the resolved thing using state::for_project for its own project; initial anywhere discovery does not authorize the response.

findings.title: Apply role module restrictions to notification reads
findings.claim: If a recipient already has task notifications and their project role is subsequently changed to turn Tasks off, those notifications remain visible and continue contributing to unread and attention counts.
findings.evidence: modules/state.rs notification predicate combines workspace switches with held project/workspace role modules_off, filtering unread and attention reads.

findings.title: Apply workspace module settings to projectless things
findings.claim: When Whiteboards is disabled in workspace A but enabled in workspace B, a member of both can still open A's workspace-wide boards through either thing endpoint.
findings.evidence: modules/things.rs shown uses viewer.workspaces[thing.organization_id] for projectless boards, rather than the anywhere union.

findings.title: Keep direct-message thread tools discoverable when Channels is off
findings.claim: With the “DMs only” or “Chat with my agents” preset, this filter removes `thread_start` and `thread_update` because their manifest owner is Channels.
findings.evidence: modules/state.rs allows_tool explicitly keeps thread_start/thread_update when Messages is on, with unit tests for the DMs-only case.

findings.title: Apply each webhook owner's effective module restrictions
findings.claim: When a webhook owner's project role turns off Automations or Tasks while the workspace switches remain on, this workspace-only check still forwards task events to their webhook.
findings.evidence: events.rs route checks workspace module switches, but webhooks.rs fan_out/visible_to check owner access and permissions without owner-effective module settings. Automations do load state::for_project. Webhook owner-role module regressions and both queue/delivery fixes remain needed.

findings.title: Preserve the reply target when flushing queued messages
findings.claim: When a reply fails with a connection error and the conversation remains open, the queued item retains `replyTo`, but `ComposerBox.flush()` reconstructs the submission without it (line 300).
findings.evidence: StructuredComposer.tsx flush passes item.replyTo with the original idempotency key; restoreQueued also restores the target.

findings.title: Preserve reply semantics when scheduling a message
findings.claim: When someone selects Reply and then uses Schedule message, the quote is silently dropped: `schedule()` still calls `onSchedule(content, at)`, and `later/api.ts::scheduleMessage` sends only `{ content, sendAt }`.
findings.evidence: StructuredComposer.tsx schedule explicitly rejects replyTo with a visible error, preserving the draft instead of silently dropping reply semantics. Full scheduled-reply support remains an intentional separate feature.

findings.title: Keep the direct thread open when jumping to an older reply target
findings.claim: In a DM/group thread panel, clicking a quote whose original is outside the loaded messages falls through to `quoted.href`.
findings.evidence: ReplyQuote.tsx uses RevealInThread when a target is not currently rendered, keeping direct thread panels open while older entries load.

findings.title: Refresh reply quotes when their source messages change
findings.claim: When a reply is on a loaded older page and its original message is edited or removed, this renders the old quote indefinitely until a reconnect or page reload.
findings.evidence: useLiveOlderEntries.ts tracks quoted-message revisions, blanks removed quotes immediately and refetches older reply quotes after edits, rather than relying only on newest-page reloads.

findings.title: Refresh reply quotes before replaying a stored send response
findings.claim: If a message is replied to and then removed, retrying the reply with its original idempotency key still returns the removed text.
findings.evidence: conversations.rs idempotency replay calls forwarding::refresh_reply_quote before responding, so removed/edited source text is not replayed from the cached body.

findings.title: Preserve resolvable references in custom-field exports
findings.claim: For page-link custom fields, `named_values` exports the page's title rather than its ID or URL.
findings.evidence: work_items/imports.rs name_field_values rewrites page references with work_item_fields::exported_page, retaining resolvable links with labels.

findings.title: Replace saved-view clauses when overriding custom-field filters
findings.claim: When `task_list` receives both a saved view and an explicit filter for the same custom field, the view's clause remains in `self.view` and is ANDed with the explicit clause here.
findings.evidence: mcp/views_data.rs apply_view removes overridden built-in clauses, but does not remove same-field custom-field clauses before mcp/tasks.rs ANDs explicit fields. Needs a saved-view override regression and field-id normalization; not fixed.

findings.title: Preserve person references through CSV formula escaping
findings.claim: When a person custom field contains someone with a handle, `named_values` exports it as `@handle`, but passing that cell through `csv_field` adds a leading apostrophe.
findings.evidence: work_items/imports.rs field_cell doubles literal leading apostrophes; unguarded removes exactly a guard or doubled quote for custom fields. Person/Text/URL/Link/SingleChoice import paths use it, while choices use JSON arrays.

findings.title: Distinguish literal apostrophes from CSV formula guards
findings.claim: For an allowed single-choice option named `'=Plan`, `csv_field` leaves the exported cell unchanged, but the new unconditional `unguarded` conversion changes it to `=Plan` on import.
findings.evidence: work_items/imports.rs field_cell doubles literal leading apostrophes; unguarded removes exactly a guard or doubled quote for custom fields. Person/Text/URL/Link/SingleChoice import paths use it, while choices use JSON arrays.

findings.title: Preserve text values through CSV formula escaping
findings.claim: When a text custom field contains `=Plan`, `@ana`, or another nonnumeric value beginning with a formula character, `tasks_csv` passes it through `csv_field`, which adds a leading apostrophe.
findings.evidence: work_items/imports.rs field_cell doubles literal leading apostrophes; unguarded removes exactly a guard or doubled quote for custom fields. Person/Text/URL/Link/SingleChoice import paths use it, while choices use JSON arrays.
